title: Karnak Temple Complex
summary: Karnak, at Thebes (modern Luxor) in Egypt, is a complex of temples centred on the precinct of the god Amun, with further precincts for Mut and Montu. Kings added to it from the Middle Kingdom through the Ptolemaic period, with Roman additions, and nearly every New Kingdom king left a mark.

uncertainty.note: Start is the reign of Intef II (c. 2112-2063 BC), the earliest evidence for Amun's temple according to Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities; the astronomical year for 2112 BC is -2111. The Ministry gives the range as approximate, hence the margin. End is the present: the complex survives as ruins.
